$comment: System invariants. These are meta-rules about the standards system itself rather than about machine-learning work, and they are NOT project-adjustable: a policy may not set their level, declare them not-applicable, write an exception against them, or attest them. Any invariant id appearing anywhere in a policy is treated as an attempted weakening. A violation produces BLOCKED_BY_INVARIANT and exit 3 — a halt rather than a score, because a compliance number computed against a tampered ruler is not a number worth publishing. See artifacts/adr/0005-integrity-invariant-enforcement.md.

rules.title: Standards are never weakened to reach a desired conclusion
rules.description: A human or AI must never bypass, weaken, remove, reclassify, reinterpret, falsify evidence for, or manipulate a standard, test, applicability determination, evidence requirement, or verification mechanism solely because it prevents the desired implementation or conclusion.
rules.rationale: The pressure this guards against is ordinary rather than exotic: a required rule fails, a deadline is close, and the cheapest path to green is to edit the rule rather than the work. An agent instructed to make the checks pass finds that path immediately, and faster than a person would. Every other guarantee in this system rests on the rules meaning today what they meant when they were reviewed.
rules.remediation: Restore what was weakened. If the change is genuinely intended, make it deliberately: update artifacts/catalog-baseline.json, record the reason in CHANGELOG.md, and version the release accordingly. The mechanism does not forbid change; it forbids invisible change.
rules.evidenceExpected: A catalog that matches its reviewed baseline, and a policy that raises no obligation below its catalog level, addresses no invariant, and dismisses no prohibition without a substantive reason.
rules.$assuranceNote: Enforced along five routes — the catalog baseline, policy weakening detection, contradicted attestations, evidence digests, and mutation tests — each closing a specific bypass. Together they establish that the recorded rules and the reviewed rules agree, and that the policy has not neutered one locally. They cannot establish intent, and they cannot detect a weakening performed by editing the baseline and the catalog together in one deliberate act; that act is visible in review because it touches the baseline, which is the property being bought.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Non-exemptible by construction. An approved exception permitting a standard to be weakened in order to reach a desired conclusion is the thing the invariant names, written down and signed.

rules.title: A rule nothing evaluated never reports as passing
rules.description: A rule that nothing evaluated is never reported as passing. Absence of a finding is not evidence of compliance, and the evaluator has no default-pass path: every route that is not an examination with no adverse finding, or a valid attestation with nothing contradicting it, ends at insufficient-evidence, not-evaluated, failed, or an invariant violation.
rules.rationale: This is the single rule the rest of the system protects. A false red has a complainant and gets fixed; a false green has none, by construction, and in this domain most rules cannot be checked at all — so the population of rules at risk of silently passing is the majority of the catalog rather than an edge case.
rules.remediation: Do not add a code path that reports passed without evidence. A rule with no mechanism belongs in neither the evaluated set nor the passing set.
rules.evidenceExpected: The evaluator's EVALUATED_RULES set agrees with its detector bindings, and every passing result carries either an examination or an attestation.
rules.$assuranceNote: Enforced by the evaluated-set gate and by engine tests asserting that unexamined rules report skipped. A new detector wired incorrectly could still bind to a rule outside the set, which is why the binding cross-check is tested in both directions.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Non-exemptible. A project-level waiver of this invariant would permit the system to report compliance it never established, which is the failure the system exists to prevent.

rules.title: Framework coverage travels beside the verdict, never inside it
rules.description: How much of the framework is machine-represented and machine-examined is reported beside the verdict and never inside it. Coverage never contributes to the status or the score, and improving coverage never improves compliance.
rules.rationale: Without this separation, COMPLIANT reads as everything was checked when it means everything checked passed. In a domain where most failures are undetectable from source text, the difference between those two sentences is most of the truth. Combining them would also create an incentive to add weak checks, since each one would raise the number.
rules.remediation: Keep frameworkCoverage out of the status computation and out of the score's numerator and denominator. Report it adjacent, with its own note.
rules.evidenceExpected: The envelope carries frameworkCoverage as a sibling of status and score, and a test confirms that changing coverage leaves both unchanged.
rules.$assuranceNote: Enforced by envelope tests. It establishes that the current code keeps the two apart; it cannot prevent a future reader from quoting the score without the coverage beside it, which is a documentation discipline rather than a mechanical one.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Non-exemptible. A project permitted to fold coverage into its score could report a high number by adding checks rather than by meeting standards.

rules.title: A heuristic conclusion is labelled as an inference
rules.description: A heuristic's conclusion is labelled INFERRED and never OBSERVED. A finding labelled OBSERVED asserts that the fact is directly verifiable at the cited location; anything reached by pattern, proximity, or naming convention is an inference and is labelled as one.
rules.rationale: A reader deciding how much weight to give a finding needs to distinguish a measurement from a guess without reading the implementation. The leakage detectors in particular are useful and are not proof, and a label is the only place that distinction survives into a summary.
rules.remediation: Label the finding INFERRED, and state in the rule's $assuranceNote what the inference does not establish.
rules.evidenceExpected: Every finding carries a label from OBSERVED, INFERRED, CONFIRMED_BY_OWNER, UNKNOWN, and heuristic detectors emit only INFERRED.
rules.$assuranceNote: Enforced by scan tests that assert heuristic findings never carry OBSERVED. The test recognises heuristics by their detector id, so a new heuristic detector added without being registered as one could evade it until the test list is updated.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Non-exemptible. Permitting a guess to be labelled as an observation is permitting the system to overstate what it knows, which is the definition of the false confidence the source brief forbids.

rules.title: Framework-generated scaffolding never satisfies the rules it was written to help meet
rules.description: An artifact this framework generates — a template written by `standards init`, or any future scaffolding — must not count as evidence that a project satisfies a substantive requirement, until a human has meaningfully completed it. A section that is empty, or contains only placeholder text, or still carries the scaffold marker, answers nothing.
rules.rationale: Observed in the first adoption against a real repository: running `standards init` flipped three required rules from failing to passed, with no work done on the project at all. The document that satisfied evaluation.baseline-exists was a table row reading “Baseline — REPLACE with the strongest simple thing that could reasonably work”. This is the standards-system form of leakage: the tool creates a placeholder, its own detector observes the placeholder, and the placeholder becomes evidence. Stated as an invariant rather than as three fixes because otherwise the same hole reopens for every template added later.
rules.remediation: Complete the document, then delete the scaffold marker. If the rule genuinely has no subject in this project, declare it not-applicable with a reason rather than leaving a template to answer for it.
rules.evidenceExpected: Documents that carry no scaffold marker and whose relevant sections contain substantive content rather than placeholders.
rules.$assuranceNote: Enforced by two independent signals — an explicit marker every generated document carries until a human removes it, and a substance check that rejects empty or placeholder-only sections. Together they establish that a document is not untouched scaffolding. They cannot establish that its content is true or adequate; a completed but wrong model card passes this and is caught, if at all, by review.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Non-exemptible. An exception here would permit the framework to accept its own output as proof that a project met a requirement, which is the purest form of the false confidence this system exists to prevent.

rules.title: What a rule accepts does not change without deliberate review
rules.description: The set of project states a machine-examined rule treats as compliant is locked in artifacts/acceptance-baseline.json and compared against the live evaluator. A state that newly passes, and a state that newly fails, are both reported and both block until the baseline is deliberately updated with its reasoning recorded.
rules.rationale: Found by trying to use the integrity check on a real change. invariant.standards-integrity locks every rule's kind, level, severity, verification method, assurance, exemptibility and attestability. Widening Standard 15 R2 from exact pins to pins-or-lock enlarged the set of compliant projects and moved none of those fields, so the guard said nothing about a change to what the standard demands. A guard that locks a rule's classification but not its satisfaction semantics cannot establish that the rule was not weakened. Strengthening is caught for a different reason: silently making existing adopters non-compliant deserves the same deliberate review as silently excusing them.
rules.remediation: Run `npm run acceptance` and read which states moved and in which direction. If the movement is intended, update artifacts/acceptance-baseline.json and record in CHANGELOG.md which states moved and why. If it is not, the change to the detector or the rule is the defect.
rules.evidenceExpected: A clean run of scripts/acceptance.mjs, or a baseline update whose reasoning is recorded in the changelog entry for the release that made it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Covers only the ten rules a mechanism examines. The other thirty-five rest on human judgement and have no observable acceptance predicate, so nothing here would detect a semantic weakening of one of them. The states are also representative rather than exhaustive: they lock the behaviour they enumerate, and a change confined to a state nobody wrote is invisible.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Non-exemptible. An exception would permit the acceptance semantics of a standard to move without anyone noticing, which is invariant.standards-integrity restated at the level this check exists to reach.
